recreation_prompt_markdown: Create a browser-based one-button endless runner called Spark Rush Roll. Present it as a neon cyber arcade game where a cute glowing spark courier automatically rolls from left to right across unstable signal rails in a digital nightscape. The player only taps, clicks, or presses to jump, and can jump only while grounded. Build the main loop around continuous forward movement, gravity, jump physics, collision with platforms, death on spikes or falling into gaps, and a camera that follows the runner. Generate the course endlessly with random gaps, varying platform lengths and heights, occasional spike-topped hazard platforms, and floating collectible charge cores above safe ground. Award score continuously for distance traveled and give extra points for collected cores. Gradually increase movement speed during each run so the challenge ramps up over time. Render the action on a full-screen canvas with a dark purple-to-black background, subtle stars, glowing grid lines, bright cyan and pink neon accents, and a round expressive player character that spins while moving and squashes or stretches during jumps and landings. Add particle bursts for jumping, pickups, and death, plus energetic background music and arcade sound effects for jump, landing, collecting, UI clicks, and failure. Surround the canvas with polished HUD and overlay screens: a start panel with title and short instructions, an in-run score display, and a game-over panel showing the final distance score with a replay button. Keep the tone fast, playful, and score-chasing, with mobile-safe full-screen controls and flashy visual feedback like brief reaction popups on pickups and crashes.
blueprint_markdown:
# Blueprint

## High-level code structure
- Single-file HTML game with embedded CSS and JavaScript.
- Presentation is split into:
  - full-screen `<canvas>` for gameplay rendering,
  - DOM-based overlay UI for start screen, HUD, game-over panel, and reaction GIFs,
  - hidden audio elements used by a small `AudioManager`.
- Core game logic lives in plain JavaScript globals and functions rather than modules.
- Config values are declared in an inline JSON script block and copied into `window.gameConfig` for runtime use.

## Game loop / state model
- Main loop uses `requestAnimationFrame(gameLoop)`.
- `gameLoop` computes delta time, calls `update(dt)`, then `draw()`.
- Primary states are:
  - attract / pre-start (`!isGameRunning && !isGameOver`),
  - active run (`isGameRunning`),
  - failure / post-run (`isGameOver`).
- `startGame()` unlocks audio, hides the start panel, shows the HUD, and calls `resetGame()`.
- `resetGame()` initializes player, score, speed, particles, platforms, and coins.
- `die()` ends the run, stops BGM, plays failure feedback, then reveals the game-over panel.

## Player goals
- Survive as long as possible while auto-running forward.
- Jump over gaps and avoid spike platforms.
- Collect floating charge-core coins for bonus points.
- Build the highest distance-based score before crashing or falling.

## Interaction pattern
- One-input action game.
- Pointer/tap on canvas triggers a jump only when grounded.
- Start and restart are handled with DOM buttons.
- The player does not steer horizontally; forward motion is automatic and speed slowly increases.

## Core systems
- Endless world generation:
  - platforms are generated ahead of the camera,
  - random gaps, platform widths, height variation, and occasional spike hazards,
  - coins spawn above some non-spike platforms.
- Physics:
  - gravity, jump force, grounded detection, fall death, simple collision checks.
- Scoring:
  - passive score gain from distance,
  - bonus points from collectible coins.
- Difficulty scaling:
  - game speed increases gradually over time.
- Juice / feedback:
  - particle bursts on jump, coin pickup, and death,
  - rotating squishy player avatar,
  - neon glow rendering and parallax grid background,
  - GIF callouts for pickup and fail moments,
  - layered UI with cyber/neon styling.
- Audio:
  - looping BGM,
  - jump / land / pickup / fail / UI click SFX,
  - synth fallback if audio playback fails.

## Inferred genre / gameplay shape
- Strongest fit: endless runner / lane-less runner with light platforming.
- Secondary traits: speed runner, neon runner, and collectible score chaser.
- The game reads like a minimalist one-button arcade survival runner with platform generation rather than a level-based platformer.

identity.title: Spark Rush Roll
identity.premise: A glowing spark courier rolls automatically across unstable neon rails, jumping over hazards and collecting charge cores in an endless cyber-themed run.
identity.interaction_model: Single-input endless runner with tap/click-to-jump controls and button-based start/restart UI.
identity.objective: Stay alive, clear gaps and spike zones, collect coins, and push the distance score as high as possible.
identity.progression: Runs begin at a moderate speed, then gradually accelerate while procedural platforms, gaps, spikes, and coin placements continue indefinitely until failure.
identity.theme: Cyber neon arcade courier run in a digital signal world.
identity.mood: Fast, bright, energetic, slightly tense, and playful.
identity.likely_audience: Casual arcade players, mobile-friendly endless runner fans, and players who enjoy quick reflex score-chasing games.
confidence_notes: High confidence that this is an endless auto-runner with one-button jumping.
High confidence that score comes from both distance and collectible coins.
Moderate confidence that the intended fantasy is a spark/signal courier traveling through a digital rail network, based on UI text and visual styling.
Low uncertainty about deeper progression beyond score-chasing; the code shows no upgrades, levels, or meta-economy.

selected_top_5.reasoning: The game auto-scrolls endlessly, generates terrain procedurally, and centers on surviving as long as possible for a higher score.
Its neon cyber palette, glowing grid backdrop, and futuristic signal-rail presentation strongly match a neon-styled runner.
Forward speed gradually increases over time, making reaction timing and maintaining pace a core challenge.
Jump timing, gravity, platform landing, gaps, and hazard collision are essential mechanics, though the game is endless rather than level-based.
It shares runner DNA and forward-only flow, but there are no discrete lanes or lane-switching mechanics, so this is only a weak resemblance.

uncertainty_notes: The game is clearly a runner, but the category universe has several overlapping runner labels, so the middle rankings involve judgment calls.
Platformer game is mechanically accurate but weaker than runner categories because the experience is not stage-based.
Sonic style runner and Train runner game were rejected because there is no franchise-specific identity, ring-style loop emphasis, or train-track lane structure.
